question.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}1-{x}^{3}, & 0\le x\le 1 \\ \frac{1}{4}, & 1<x\le 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{5}].$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the fifth raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{5}] & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{5}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{5}\cdot (1-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{5}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{5}-{x}^{8})\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\frac{1}{6}\,{x}^{6}-\frac{1}{9}\,{x}^{9}){|}_{0}^{1}+\frac{1}{24}\,{x}^{6}\,{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{9}-0)+\frac{1}{24}(64-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{18}+\frac{21}{8} \\  & =\frac{193}{72}\end{aligned}
$$
